Description: Auftraggeber (AG) ist das Jobcenter Berlin Mitte, eine gemeinsame Einrichtung der Agentur für Arbeit Berlin Mitte und des Bezirksamt Mitte von Berlin zur Erfüllung des gesetzlichen Auftrages nach dem SGB II (§ 44b, § 6d SGB II). Dafür unterhält das Jobcenter Berlin Mitte angemietete Büroflächen an verschiedenen Standorten (Liegenschaften), im Kapweg 3-5 in 13405 Berlin, in der Seydelstr. 2-5 in 10117 Berlin, in der Lehrter Str. 46 in 10557 Berlin, in der Müllerstr. 16 und Müllerstr. 147 in 13353 Berlin. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Ziel der Vergabe ist der Abschluss eines Vertrages über das Betreiben der Poststellen und die Hauspostverteilung zur Sicherstellung eines ordnungsgemäßen „erweiterten Postumlaufs“ (Posteingang und Postausgang, Bearbeitung von Päckchen und Paketen, Botendienst innerhalb der Dienststelle, weitere Postdienstleistungen) in den Liegenschaften des Jobcenter Berlin Mitte. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Vor Erstellung und Abgabe des Angebotes hat sich der Bieter zwingend durch eine verpflichtende Besichtigung aller betroffenen Objekte über die örtlichen Gegebenheiten zu informieren. Dies bestätigt der Bieter mit seiner Unterschrift im Angebotsschreiben sowie dem mit Angebotsabgabe einzureichenden Formblatt „Nachweis der Objektbesichtigung“. Spätere Einreden wegen besonderer örtlicher Gegebenheiten werden nicht anerkannt. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Anmeldungen zur Objektbesichtigung erfolgen per E-Mail an: Jobcenter-Berlin-Mitte.Verwaltung@jobcenter-ge.de --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Angebot von Bietern, die nicht an der Objektbesichtigung teilgenommen haben, werden im Verfahren nicht berücksichtigt. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Der Anmeldeschluss zur Objektbesichtigung ist Mittwoch, 16. normalized.title: I-HAB Harness (HRNS)
normalized.description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. 
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. 
It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Harness (HRNS) for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Harness (HRNS) are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The harness (HRNS) function is to provide distribution and separation of power, analogue and digital signal, commands and lines to the different unit and/or interface. 
The harness will include the following items:
	Cables and connectors required to perform the electrical links
	Shielding provisions for the wiring
	Over shielding provision for the bundles when deemed necessary by EMC engineering for fulfilling magnetic and electrical fields cleanliness requirements or to limit dielectric charging from high energy electrons surrounding the spacecraft.

normalized.title: Study to assess Out-of-Court Dispute Settlement (ODS) bodies under Article 21 of the Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act)
normalized.description:
The Digital Services Act (DSA) introduces certified out-of-court dispute settlement (ODS) bodies under Article 21 to enhance user redress mechanisms beyond internal complaint systems and judicial proceedings. These bodies offer users a neutral and independent forum for resolving disputes related to content moderation decisions by online platforms. Recognising the novelty and complexity of this mechanism, this study is dedicated to supporting the implementation of Article 21 by analysing cooperation between certified ODS bodies and online platforms. It will address both practical and legal challenges, including the assessment of case admissibility, information exchange, technical constraints, and financial considerations. By examining current practices and gathering feedback from stakeholders, the study aims to develop actionable recommendations to improve the ODS process.

The study’s findings will support the European Commission, the Digital Services Coordinators, and the European Board for Digital Services in their supervision and enforcement roles. Special attention will be given to challenges faced during the post-certification phase, drawing from experiences across Member States and a range of platform types and ODS bodies. The study will not only focus on legal obligations and procedural fairness but also on technical interoperability and case management models. Ultimately, it aims to foster more transparent and effective cooperation between platforms and ODS bodies, promote fairer content moderation, and reinforce user trust in digital services.
